system.name: Study Coach
system.description: A local study coach for Microsoft certification exams, starting with AZ-104: AI instructors teach each skill and the learner practises with original, documentation-checked questions

people.name: Learner
people.description: Studies for AZ-104: takes lessons, practises questions, reads the docs and fact sheets

people.name: Content maintainer
people.description: Syncs the docs, builds fact sheets and generates the question bank from the command line (the same person as the learner)

containers.name: Web app
containers.description: Home, Room (live lesson), Practice, Coverage and Docs screens in the browser; proxies /api and /agents to the server

containers.name: Coach server
containers.technology: Node.js, Hono, Flue 2.3 runtime (vite dev on 127.0.0.1:8787)
containers.description: Hosts the Coach agent (lead plus specialist subagents) behind Flue's agent router and the coach JSON API for skills, sessions, practice, answers, coverage and docs

containers.name: Content pipeline
containers.description: docs:sync, docs:sheets, docs:review, generate and the questions:* commands (export, lint, review, reverify): syncs the Microsoft docs repos, runs the FactSheetWriter, FactSheetReviewer, QuestionWriter and QuestionReverifier agents as child processes (one per sheet, review, question or batch), and exports, lints and imports the committed question bank

containers.name: Coach database
containers.description: Skills, areas, verified questions, sessions, attempts, flags and cached Learn pages; shared by the server and generation runs; a new database loads the committed question bank on first run

containers.name: Conversation store
containers.description: Durable Flue conversations for lessons; batch runs use an in-memory store instead

containers.name: Docs corpus and fact sheets
containers.description: Markdown-only sparse clones of five MicrosoftDocs repos (azure-docs, azure-compute-docs, azure-management-docs, azure-monitor-docs, entra-docs), one committed fact sheet per skill that the writer, verifier and reviewer read, and the committed question bank (content/questions, one JSON file per skill)

external_systems.name: MiniMax API
external_systems.description: Language model (MiniMax-M3 by default; M3.1 Flash is used for the fact-sheet reviewer) for every role: lead, specialists, writer, verifier, fact-sheet writer and reviewer

external_systems.name: Microsoft Learn
external_systems.description: Live documentation pages, fetched and cached when a page is not in the local corpus or when its local copy is missing includes from Microsoft's private reusable-content repo

external_systems.name: MicrosoftDocs on GitHub
external_systems.description: Source repositories (azure-docs, azure-compute-docs, azure-management-docs, azure-monitor-docs, entra-docs) cloned sparsely into the local corpus

summary.overview: Study Coach is a single-user application run locally. A React web app talks to one Node server that hosts a Flue Coach agent (a lead instructor delegating to per-area specialist subagents) and a Hono JSON API over a SQLite database. A separate command-line pipeline syncs the Microsoft documentation into a local corpus, builds a fact sheet per skill and generates the question bank by running a writer agent once per question, and a reviewer agent checks each fact-sheet bullet against the page it cites, while a re-checker agent answers stored questions from the current sheet to catch ones whose key no longer holds. The verified questions are committed as JSON and load into a fresh database on first run, admitting a question only after a leak check and an independent verifier agree with its key. Every model call goes to MiniMax (M3 by default; M3.1 Flash is available). Generation retries a slow or failing question once on a fallback model and logs each call's tokens and cost.
findings: Every role defaults to one provider, `minimax/MiniMax-M3` (`src/coach/models.ts:1`, fallbacks at `src/coach/models.ts:16`). Generation retries a question that times out or ends in a model error once on a fallback model (`scripts/generate.ts:141`, flag at `scripts/generate.ts:258`), but a used-up usage window (a 429, "usage limit reached") stops generation after about an hour and twenty minutes of work and stops lessons outright, which have no fallback at all.

The server and generation runs share `data/coach.db`; this is handled with WAL and a 5 s busy timeout (`src/coach/db.ts:91-92`). Flue's own store has no such setting, so batch runs avoid it with an in-memory store (`scripts/flue-jobs.ts:119`), which means generation conversations are not kept.
The scaffold `Assistant` agent is still mounted at `/agents/assistant` with a hard-coded model (`src/app.ts:14`, `src/agents/assistant.ts:8`); nothing in the web app uses it.

There is no authentication on `/api` or `/agents` (`src/app.ts:11-16`); safety rests on the dev server binding to 127.0.0.1 (`package.json:17`). There is no production build or start script, only `vite dev`.

Adding an area touches several places: skills in `src/coach/exam/seed.ts`, instructors in `src/coach/exam/instructors.ts` and `web/src/lib/instructors.ts`, colour tokens in `web/src/styles.css` and diagram nouns in `src/coach/diagram-schema.ts`. The earlier import cycle between instructors and seed is gone: `src/coach/exam/seed.ts` no longer imports the instructors.

The lead's tools and hand-overs are gated by a read-only "learner has the floor" flag (`src/tools/coach-tools.ts:185`, `src/agents/coach.ts:69`). Flue renders a subagent at delegation time and throws on any state write during a render, so the check must never write. An earlier version wrote there, and every hand-over failed while the evals still passed because they checked only speaker names; the eval now fails on any failed hand-over (`src/evals/coach.eval.ts:85`).

Generation runs each question as its own `flue run` process (`scripts/flue-jobs.ts:123`), so usage is recorded from inside the agent module through Flue's `observe()` (`src/coach/usage-log.ts:55`) and tied to the run by `GENERATE_RUN_ID` (`scripts/generate.ts:214`); the verifier's scratch conversation would otherwise be counted separately.

The committed question bank is unreviewed: the `reviewed` flag exists on every question (`src/coach/questions/question-bank.ts:20`) but only a person sets it, and the fact sheets are checked by a model reviewer whose findings differ between runs (`src/agents/fact-sheet-reviewer.ts:25`), so a clean result is not proof.

A skill page is read from the local docs when its includes all resolve, and live from Learn otherwise (`src/coach/docs/corpus.ts:135`). 17 pages across 16 skills use includes from Microsoft's private reusable-content repo, so they are read live; 10 more pages (`.yml` pages in private repos, three Entra licensing pages that now redirect to Microsoft 365 docs, one support-repo page) are always live. A live read can return a partial page, which made the reviewer flag correct bullets, so sheets for those pages are the least checkable.

Every tab of a tabbed page is now kept under a label, and a tab group ends at any line of three or more dashes (`src/coach/docs/doc-markdown.ts:64`). Before this, only the first tab was kept and the rest of the page was cut at the first longer terminator, so the sheet writer and the reviewer could not see CLI and PowerShell steps; pages and sheets built before the change may still reflect that.

A stored question is only as good as the sheet it was verified against: the writer's verifier reads the sheet, not the pages, so a sheet error reaches the bank. `questions:reverify` re-answers a skill's questions from the current sheet without the keys (`src/coach/questions/reverify.ts:40`) and found one unsupported question in the 20 for `compute.vm-sizes`; it has been run on that one skill only.
recommendations: Extend the fallback model to lessons, and to a usage-limit 429, so a used-up plan does not stop lessons.
Remove the scaffold Assistant route, or stop mounting it, since nothing uses it.
Keep the server bound to localhost; add authentication before exposing it on any other interface.
Run the fact-sheet reviewer more than once, or on a second provider's model, and treat bullets citing live-read pages as unchecked rather than unsupported.
Derive the web instructor list and colours from the server catalog (for example via /api/skills) so a new area is data in one place.

Run `questions:reverify` on every skill whose fact sheet was rebuilt or corrected after its questions were written, and keep the corrected sheets out of a plain `docs:sheets` run, which would overwrite them.
